div.head: Norðleoda 7
div.ab: 7 gif Wilisc man geþeo, þæt he hæbbe hywisc landes 7 mage cynges gafel forðbringan, þonne byð his wergyld CCXX scll'.
Et si Waliscus promoueatur, ut habeat familiam et terram et possit gablum regis reddere, tunc est wera eius CCXX sol.
And gif Wilisman geþeo, þæt he hæbbe hiwisc landes 7 mæge cyninges gafol forðbringan, þonne bið his wergild CXX scill'.
And if a Welshman prospers, that he has a hide of land and may produce the king's tribute, then his wergild is 120 shillings.
And if a Welshman prospers so that he possesses a hide of land and can pay the king's tribute, then his wergild shall be two hundred and twenty shillings.
Und wenn ein Wälscher [so] emporkommt, dass er 1 Hid Landes besitzt und Steuer [direct] an den König aufzubringen vermag, dann ist sein Wergeld 120 Schill. (220 hlq).
And if a Welshman prospers [so] that he holds 1 hide of land and can pay tax [directly] to the king, then his wergild is 120 shillings (220, hlq).
div.note: D reads CXX; H's CCXX is a corruption in hlq (likewise below Mirce 3). Liebermann notes that clauses 7–12 are, according to Schmid, a later extension, probably southern-English influenced. Ld: ‘a Welshman's wergild, if he has become so rich that he has a household and property and can pay the king tax: it is 220 shillings’. Liebermann compares Ine 32.
